name: Amwaste LLC
subsector: Solid waste collection, transfer, landfill, and recycling
description: Amwaste provides non-hazardous solid waste collection, transfer, landfill, and recycling services in the Southeastern United States. Its customer base includes residential, commercial, construction and industrial end markets across Alabama, Georgia, and Louisiana. The business operates an asset-heavy, vertically integrated model supported by owned disposal sites, transfer stations, and recycling infrastructure. Public materials describe a platform with more than 300,000 customers, eight landfill sites, ten transfer stations, and a materials recovery facility. The company has expanded through bolt-on acquisitions and local contract wins to deepen density in its core Southeastern markets. 3i invested growth capital through the 3i North American Infrastructure Fund in July 2023, and current ownership percentages are not publicly disclosed.

name: Regional Rail, LLC
description: Regional Rail owns and operates short-line freight railroads and related rail services across the United States and Canada. Its customer base spans industrial, agricultural, chemicals, aggregates, food, and logistics end markets that depend on local freight connectivity and transload services. The company follows an asset-heavy operating model built around owned and leased track, rail-served industrial infrastructure, and operating railroad franchises. name: JVR Energy Park
description: JVR Energy Park is a co-located solar and battery storage project in southeastern San Diego County. Its customer base is San Diego Community Power and the California grid, which will receive contracted renewable energy and storage capacity from the project. The project follows an asset-heavy contracted operating model based on utility-scale generation and storage infrastructure. Public disclosures describe a 90 megawatt AC solar facility paired with a 70 megawatt AC and 280 megawatt-hour battery storage system, with expected output sufficient to serve about 57,000 homes. BayWa r.e. developed the project and closed full financing in 2025 as it advanced toward commercial operations in 2026. Acadia participated through preferred equity in the 2025 financing package, while BayWa r.e. remains the disclosed project sponsor and developer.

name: Peregrine Energy Storage Project
description: Peregrine is a utility-scale battery storage facility in the Barrio Logan area of San Diego. Its customer base is the California power system, where the project provides energy shifting, capacity, and grid-reliability services rather than retail electricity supply. The facility follows an asset-heavy storage-infrastructure model centered on a standalone battery project connected to the local transmission system. Public disclosures describe a 200 megawatt and 400 megawatt-hour lithium-ion battery system that became Arevon's fifth operating utility-scale storage facility in California. The project reached commercial operation in 2025 after Arevon closed a project financing package that included debt, tax equity, and preferred equity components. Acadia's role was publicly described as sourcing preferred equity for the financing, while Arevon remained the disclosed developer, owner, and operator.

name: Boldyn Networks

description: I-66 Express Mobility Partners, LLC is the private concessionaire and operator of the 66 Express Outside the Beltway managed lanes in Northern Virginia, also known as Transform 66 Outside the Beltway. description: AFCO develops, finances, leases, and manages on-airport cargo and other aviation facilities. Its customers include airlines, freight forwarders, ground handlers, and airport users that require specialized airport-adjacent infrastructure. The business follows an asset-heavy model built around long-duration aviation real estate and operating platforms at multiple airports. Public company materials state that AFCO manages more than 3.5 million square feet across 29 properties at 15 airport locations in North America and the United Kingdom. AFCO was founded in 1992, Goldman Sachs Alternatives acquired the company in 2018, and Ardian announced in February 2025 that it had signed an agreement to acquire Goldman Sachs Alternatives' stake.

name: CampusParc
ownershipVehicle: Ardian Americas Infrastructure Fund V (AAIF V)
description: CampusParc is the concessionaire that manages, operates, and maintains the parking system at The Ohio State University. Its customer base includes students, faculty, staff, visitors, and users of the Wexner Medical Center campus. The business operates under a long-term concession model in which parking revenues support operations, maintenance, and capital obligations across the system. Public disclosures describe more than 37,000 parking spaces across garages, surface lots, and metered spaces under a 50-year concession in Columbus, Ohio. CampusParc was formed in 2012, originally by QIC and LAZ Parking, and Ardian acquired a 100 percent stake from funds managed by QIC in June 2024 through AAIF V.

name: Clermont
ownershipVehicle: Ardian Americas Infrastructure Fund V (AAIF V)
description: Clermont is a Canadian parking investment platform formed by Ardian and Indigo Group. The platform is intended to acquire and manage parking assets, concessions, and long-term leases serving municipalities, institutions, and commercial customers across Canada. Its operating model combines long-duration parking rights with Indigo's operating capabilities and local market coverage. Public launch materials describe Clermont as a dedicated national vehicle for further parking investments in Canada, with Indigo continuing to manage operations. Ardian stated that the Clermont transaction would be made through Ardian Americas Infrastructure Fund V (AAIF V). Clermont was created in March 2024 by Ardian and Indigo Group as a new joint venture, and the detailed ownership split has not been publicly disclosed.

name: Maple Leaf
description: Maple Leaf is the battery storage joint venture formed by Ardian and Enel X in Canada. The platform provides grid services through utility-scale battery assets in Ontario and serves the provincial power system. Its operating model is asset-heavy and based on contracted and market-based storage revenues from a portfolio of operating sites. At launch, the venture comprised ten battery storage sites in Ontario with about 30 MW of aggregate capacity. Ardian and Enel X launched Maple Leaf in September 2020 with an 80 percent and 20 percent ownership split, respectively.

description: MXT Holdings develops, owns, and operates neutral-host telecommunications infrastructure in Mexico, including towers and metropolitan fiber assets. Its customers are mobile network operators and other communications users that require shared infrastructure rather than single-tenant proprietary networks. The operating model is asset-heavy and lease driven, with recurring revenue tied to long-lived telecom sites and network infrastructure. The platform is focused on Mexico and is positioned around neutral-host infrastructure that supports carrier densification and connectivity demand. Ardian announced in 2023 that it had acquired a 50% co-control equity interest in MXT Holdings, which it described as its first direct investment in Mexico.

name: Rover Pipeline
description: Rover Pipeline LLC is a large-scale interstate natural gas transmission system connecting Marcellus and Utica production in Pennsylvania and West Virginia with demand markets across Ohio, Michigan and the broader Midwest. description: Énergir distributes natural gas and related energy services in Quebec and Vermont and is expanding activities in renewable natural gas, energy efficiency, and other low-carbon infrastructure. Its customer base includes residential, commercial, industrial, and institutional users served through regulated utility operations and related energy platforms. The business is asset-heavy and largely regulated because it depends on long-lived distribution networks, storage assets, and contracted infrastructure rather than merchant commodity exposure alone. Public company materials identify Quebec as the principal operating market, with an additional gas utility footprint in Vermont and renewable energy interests elsewhere in North America. CDPQ increased its stake in 2022 through Trencap L.P., after which the company disclosed ownership of 80.9% by CDPQ and 19.1% by Fonds de solidarité FTQ.

description: ICA OVT is an operating platform for Mexican transport concessions, focused on toll road and tunnel assets. name: Indiana Toll Road
description: Indiana Toll Road operates the tolled east-west highway corridor across northern Indiana. Its users are passenger and freight vehicles that pay tolls for access to a major interstate transportation route. The business is asset-heavy and concession-based because value depends on a long-lived roadway asset, traffic demand, and concession rights rather than contracted utility-style revenues. name: Vineyard Wind 1
description: Vineyard Wind 1 is an 800 MW offshore wind project off Massachusetts and is widely described as the first commercial-scale offshore wind project in the United States. The asset serves New England power demand under contracted utility offtake arrangements and associated transmission infrastructure. The model is asset-heavy because it involves offshore lease rights, marine construction, export transmission, and long-term operation of a large offshore generation asset. CIP project materials state that financial close occurred in 2021, first power was delivered in late 2023 and early 2024 announcements confirmed the start of power delivery, with full operations targeted thereafter. Public ownership disclosures identify a joint ownership structure between CIP and Avangrid, while exact percentages are not disclosed in the sources reviewed.

name: 407 ETR
description: 407 ETR operates an all-electronic toll highway across the Greater Toronto Area. Its customers are passenger and commercial vehicle users seeking time savings on a major east-west corridor, and revenue is generated from tolling and related roadway services. The business is asset-heavy and concession-based because performance depends on a long-life road network, traffic volumes, toll policy, and maintenance of the concession asset. Company disclosures state that the highway extends 108 kilometres and that 407 International became the owner of the concession company in 1999. CPP Investments has been an investor in 407 International since 2010, when it acquired control of a 40% holding through two separate transactions; later 2019 and 2025 transactions changed ownership percentages but did not reset CPP Investments' original owner-entry year. Public ownership disclosures show that, following 2025 transactions, Ferrovial owns 48.29%, CPP Investments and other institutional investors own 44.20%, and PSP Investments owns 7.51%.

name: Pacifico Sur
description: Pacifico Sur is the operating toll-road concession held through Concesionaria Autopista Guadalajara Tepic, S.A. de C.V. (CAGT). Its 309.6-kilometer network in Jalisco and Nayarit includes the Guadalajara–Tepic toll road, the South Guadalajara Bypass and the Tepic Bypass, serving freight, tourism and other toll-paying road users under a long-duration user-pay concession. A definitive agreement was announced on October 2, 2018 and the direct purchase of 49% of CAGT closed on May 15, 2019, leaving IDEAL with 51%, CPP Investments with 29% and Ontario Teachers' with 20%. A 2020 modification extended the concession to 60 years from November 30, 2011, implying expiry in November 2071. description: Redaptive provides energy-as-a-service financing and execution for building-efficiency, renewable-power, and related decarbonization projects. Its customers are enterprise and institutional building owners that seek lower energy use and infrastructure upgrades without funding the full upfront capital cost themselves. name: Sempra Infrastructure Partners, LP
subsector: LNG export, gas infrastructure, and low-carbon energy infrastructure
description: Sempra Infrastructure develops and operates LNG, energy networks, and lower-carbon infrastructure across North America. Its customer base includes utilities, LNG buyers, industrial counterparties, and other energy-market participants, and its operating model combines long-lived, asset-heavy infrastructure with a mix of contracted services and commodity-linked activity. The platform is headquartered in Houston and its principal assets and development projects are concentrated in Texas, Louisiana, and Mexico. Public disclosures describe the business as one of North America's larger private energy infrastructure platforms, anchored by LNG export, pipeline, storage, and related assets. Sempra completed the sale of a 30% non-controlling interest in Sempra Infrastructure to KKR and ADIA on June 1, 2022, leaving Sempra with a 70% controlling stake. In September 2025, Sempra announced an agreement that would change the ownership structure, but the company still described the 70%/20%/10% structure as current pending that future closing.

name: Transurban Chesapeake
description: Transurban Chesapeake LLC is the concession platform that owns the entities operating the 495, 95 and 395 Express Lanes in Northern Virginia, including the Fredericksburg Extension and 495 NEXT. It develops, finances, operates and maintains dynamically priced express lanes serving motorists, high-occupancy vehicles, buses and permitted commercial traffic in partnership with VDOT. name: Vantage Data Centers
description: Vantage Data Centers develops, owns, manages and operates hyperscale data-center campuses for cloud, AI, internet and large-enterprise customers. Founded in 2010 and headquartered in Denver, the global platform includes substantial United States and Canadian operations. This canonical record consolidates direct platform equity and manager-level North American co-investments while treating Vantage SDC as a stabilized 12-asset North American portfolio managed and operated by Vantage rather than as a separate company. DigitalBridge has held platform equity since the March 2017 acquisition and led the closed $9.2 billion 2024 recapitalization with Silver Lake. CBRE participated first in pre-SDC platform equity and then in the current Vantage SDC portfolio; DigitalBridge separately retains a 12.8% SDC interest. Pantheon Infrastructure plc has a current $34.7 million North American co-investment, GCM Grosvenor retains its disclosed growth-platform exposure, and PSP exited the North American and EMEA development platforms in 2024 while disclosing a residual Vantage interest. name: Cornerstone Generation
description: Cornerstone Generation owns a portfolio of PJM gas-fired generation assets consisting of Waterford in Ohio, Lawrenceburg in Indiana, and Darby in Ohio. Its customers are wholesale power markets and capacity markets, and its earnings profile is therefore more merchant than contracted compared with regulated or availability-based infrastructure businesses. The platform is asset-heavy and ECP has described it as a 2.5 GW or approximately 2.6 GW fleet across the three facilities. Public deal materials show that ECP acquired the business as a carve-out of Lightstone Generation from Blackstone and ArcLight in a deal announced in September 2024 and closed in early 2025, and later agreed to sell it to Talen in 2026, subject to regulatory approvals. Pending completion of that sale, Cornerstone remains an ECP-backed merchant generation platform in the Midwest PJM market.

name: Trenton Biogas
subsector: Food-waste anaerobic digestion and renewable power
description: Trenton Biogas is a food-waste anaerobic digestion facility that processes organic waste and converts it into renewable power and related byproducts. Its customers include food waste generators and other waste counterparties in the tri-state region, and the operating model is asset-heavy with tipping-fee revenues and energy production from a dedicated processing plant. Official company materials state that the facility began operations in 2019 and is designed to process about 110,000 tons of food waste per year. Equilibrium's 2020 sustainability materials identify Trenton Biogas as a Water-Waste-Energy partner and state that WWE enabled the site's repurposing, but the reviewed public materials do not clearly disclose current equity ownership percentages or the original investment date.

name: North Carolina Solar
description: North Carolina Solar is one five-project operating solar portfolio in North Carolina comprising Brantley, Fox Creek, Buckleberry, Innovative Solar 54 and Innovative Solar 67. John Laing's portfolio page reports 334 MWdc across the five assets, with contracted power sales to Duke Energy Progress and commercial operations beginning from late 2018 into early 2019. John Laing assembled the portfolio in 2018. KKR acquired John Laing Group in September 2021, and Equitix completed its 50% investment in John Laing Investments Limited on October 6, 2021. Direct April 2026 evidence describes JLIL as 50:50 owned by Equitix and KKR-owned John Laing Group. The historic 9.9% ProjectCo/HoldCo minority and its current rights are not publicly disclosed and are not inferred to be tax equity. Granite is a separate eight-project portfolio and is excluded from this company boundary. No later portfolio sale or signed pending ownership transaction was identified through August 29, 2026.

name: Rio Grande LNG
description: Rio Grande LNG is a large-scale LNG liquefaction and export terminal under construction at the Port of Brownsville, Texas. NextDecade operates the project, which is planned for approximately 30 million tonnes per annum across five trains and serves global long-term LNG offtakers. Phase 1 closed on July 12, 2023 with equity from Global Infrastructure Partners, GIC, Mubadala, TotalEnergies and NextDecade. The same investor group participated in later Train 4 and Train 5 transactions through separate project vehicles. XRG subsequently acquired partial GIP interests: 11.7% of Phase 1 and 7.6% across Trains 4 and 5. GIP remains an active investor after those partial sell-downs. BlackRock's October 2024 acquisition of GIP did not create a separate Rio Grande LNG ownership period. At June 2026, Trains 1 and 2 were 74.0% complete, Train 3 was 50.4%, Train 4 was 15.5% and Train 5 was 9.4%, with first Train 1 LNG expected in the first half of 2027. Train and holding entities are treated as project vehicles beneath the one terminal record. No signed pending company-level exit was identified through August 23, 2026.

XRG completed a second acquisition from a GIP vehicle, taking a 7.6% aggregate interest across Trains 4 and 5 while GIP retained a residual stake.
NextDecade reported Trains 1 and 2 at 74.0% completion, Train 3 at 50.4%, Train 4 at 15.5% and Train 5 at 9.4%, with first Train 1 LNG expected in the first half of 2027.

name: Terra-Gen
subsector: Utility-scale wind, solar, and battery storage
description: Terra-Gen develops, owns and operates utility-scale wind, solar and battery-storage assets across the United States. Public disclosures through July 2026 describe approximately 4.2 GW of gross operating capacity, 5.6 GWh of storage, 34 sites and a roughly 16 GW development pipeline. Terra-Gen Power Holdings II, LLC is the parent platform, Terra-Gen, LLC is the operating business and individual project SPVs remain subordinate assets. subsector: Nature-based carbon removal and forest carbon projects
description: Chestnut Carbon develops nature-based carbon removal projects focused on afforestation and improved forest management in the United States. Its customers are corporations and other organizations purchasing verified carbon removal or offset credits as part of climate and sustainability programs. The operating model is land and project intensive, built around long-dated forestry project development, ecological stewardship, measurement, and monetization of verified carbon credits. Public company materials state that Chestnut was founded by Kimmeridge in 2022 and combines forestry, carbon-market, and land-management expertise to develop U.S. forest carbon projects. Kimmeridge launched and capitalized the platform through its carbon solutions strategy and announced a strategic acquisition of Forest Carbon Works at launch.

name: Common Energy
subsector: Community solar customer acquisition and clean-energy services
description: Common Energy helps households, businesses, nonprofits, and institutions participate in community solar and related clean-energy programs. Its end markets are retail and organizational electricity users that want bill savings and renewable-energy participation without owning on-site generation. The operating model is more service and platform oriented than a pure asset-owning utility, connecting customers to community solar subscriptions and other clean-energy offerings across multiple states. Public company materials reference community solar enrollment, power purchase agreement support, and more than 10 billion kilowatt-hours of load analyses as part of the platform's customer offering. Reviewed public materials indicate Kimmeridge Carbon Solutions had invested in Common Energy by September 2023, but detailed current ownership terms and the exact transaction date were not publicly disclosed.

name: LandGate
description: LandGate provides data, analytics, and marketplace tools for renewable energy, natural gas, carbon, and infrastructure site selection and development. Its customers include developers, capital providers, landowners, and commercial counterparties evaluating infrastructure opportunities and land-resource economics. The operating model is software and data oriented rather than asset-heavy, generating value through proprietary datasets, analytics, and transaction or subscription-driven services. Public company materials describe solutions for site selection, origination, financing, and market analysis across renewables, data centers, energy storage, EV infrastructure, and natural gas. LandGate raised a Series B funding round in 2022 that included participation from Kimmeridge.

name: SYSO Technologies
subsector: Renewable asset operations and market optimization software
description: SYSO Technologies provides software and market operations services for renewable energy and battery storage assets. Its customers are asset owners, developers, and operators that need dispatch, revenue optimization, and day-to-day market participation support for renewable and storage fleets. The operating model is more software and services based than a traditional asset-owning utility, although the platform is directly tied to the performance of physical generation and storage infrastructure. Public company materials describe SYSO as a market operator of renewable energy and battery storage assets and stated in 2024 that the company had raised Series B funding led by Kimmeridge to expand gigawatts under management. Kimmeridge led SYSO's $14.5 million Series B round in 2024, and a 2026 extension increased the total Series B financing to $15.5 million.

name: AEP Transmission Company
description: AEP Transmission Company develops, owns, and operates high-voltage electric transmission infrastructure through transmission-only utility subsidiaries. Its end markets are electric load-serving utilities, wholesale power networks, and end users that depend on reliable grid expansion and interconnection capacity. The operating model is asset-heavy and regulated, with returns tied to transmission rate base growth and FERC-regulated utility frameworks rather than merchant power sales. Public disclosures for the 2025 transaction describe the investment as covering AEP's Ohio and Indiana Michigan transmission companies, which support AEP's large utility footprint and capital plan. AEP announced in January 2025, and closed in June 2025, a 19.9% equity investment in these transmission companies by KKR and PSP Investments through a joint strategic partnership.

name: Coastal GasLink Pipeline
description: Coastal GasLink Pipeline Project is a 670-kilometre natural gas transmission project connecting northeastern British Columbia to LNG Canada’s export terminal in Kitimat. description: Metronet builds and operates fiber broadband networks that provide internet and related connectivity services to residential, business, and wholesale customers. Its end markets include households, enterprises, and service providers seeking fiber-to-the-premise access in underserved and expanding U.S. communities. description: Monterra Energy is a Mexican natural gas transportation and distribution platform serving industrial, commercial, and other gas users. Its customer base is tied to essential fuel delivery for industrial operations and other end users that require physical gas infrastructure rather than merchant trading alone. The operating model is asset-heavy and midstream oriented, with value tied to pipeline and gas-delivery infrastructure. name: Brazos Midstream
subsector: Natural gas gathering, processing, and crude oil infrastructure
ownershipVehicle: North Haven Infrastructure Partners II (NHIP II)
description: Brazos Midstream provides natural gas gathering, processing, compression, and related crude and water infrastructure services in the Permian Basin. Its customers are upstream producers, and the business follows an asset-heavy, predominantly contracted midstream model built around gathering systems and processing plants. Company materials state that Brazos was founded in 2014 and now operates across both the Delaware and Midland Basins. Public disclosures reviewed in 2025 and 2026 describe expansion in the Midland Basin, including approximately 525 miles of gathering pipeline and 16 compressor stations expected by mid-2026, together with up to 800 MMcf/d of operated processing capacity by late 2026. The 2018 Delaware Basin transaction identified North Haven Infrastructure Partners II (NHIP II), an investment fund managed by Morgan Stanley Infrastructure, as the buyer, while later materials describe Morgan Stanley Infrastructure Partners as a majority investor in Brazos Midstream Holdings II. The business continues to expand processing and gathering capacity to serve producer activity in West Texas.

name: Brightspeed
ownershipVehicle: Apollo-managed funds (including AIOF II Connect Holdings, L.P.)
description: Brightspeed owns and operates wireline telecommunications and fiber broadband infrastructure across 20 U.S. states from Charlotte, North Carolina. Apollo-managed funds completed the acquisition of Lumen's incumbent local exchange carrier operations in October 2022. name: Transportation Equipment Network
description: Transportation Equipment Network (TEN) is an asset-owning North American commercial-trailer leasing and fleet-services platform serving carriers, shippers and logistics operators. name: Altius Renewable Royalties Corp.
description: Altius Renewable Royalties acquires and manages royalty interests tied to wind, solar, and other renewable energy projects. Its customers are effectively renewable project owners and developers that monetize a portion of future project revenues in exchange for growth capital, making the model contractual and asset-light rather than owner-operator based. name: Blueprint Data Centers
description: Blueprint Data Centers is a U.S. data center development platform focused on new campus delivery for hyperscale and large enterprise demand. description: AMAROK installs, operates, monitors, and maintains electric fencing and related perimeter security infrastructure for commercial and industrial properties. description: Pelican Pipeline is a new-build natural gas transmission project being developed in Louisiana. The separate proposed Energy Center repowering was denied, its applications were withdrawn in 2024, and it was not built.

name: NorthLink Aviation
description: NorthLink Aviation LLC is developing a dedicated air-cargo campus on 120 acres at Ted Stevens Anchorage International Airport under a 55-year state lease. description: This joint venture owns three stabilized hyperscale data center buildings in Northern Virginia. Its customers are investment-grade hyperscale users that require large-scale leased capacity in one of the deepest data center markets in the United States. description: Sparkfund develops and manages distributed energy deployment programs and energy-as-a-service offerings for utilities, energy companies, and building owners. Its customer base spans utilities, energy majors, and large-load or commercial hosts that need distributed assets deployed at scale to support grid and building use cases. The company operates a contracted, service-led model that coordinates program design, host engagement, asset deployment, and value-chain management rather than merchant power sales. Public materials describe more than a decade of operating history and a national role in distributed capacity procurement and other distributed energy resource deployment programs. Vision Ridge invested in the platform and continues to identify Sparkfund as an active portfolio company focused on scaling distributed energy infrastructure in the built environment.

name: TeraWatt Infrastructure
description: TeraWatt Infrastructure develops, owns, and operates charging sites and related energy infrastructure for commercial electric vehicle fleets, autonomous fleets, and heavy-duty transport users. Its customers are fleet operators and logistics users that need property, charging equipment, energy management, and ongoing site operations delivered as a single infrastructure solution. The platform is asset-heavy, with owned and developed real estate, charging systems, and associated energy infrastructure supporting long-term fleet deployment rather than one-time equipment sales. Public materials describe the company as operating the nation's largest portfolio of purpose-built commercial EV charging sites and as expanding in major U.S. freight and fleet corridors. Sustainable Asset Fund III is one of TeraWatt's backers, and the company raised more than $1 billion in 2022 to accelerate national buildout after emerging publicly in 2021.

name: Gulf Coast Express Pipeline LLC (GCX)
description: Gulf Coast Express Pipeline LLC (GCX) is an approximately 500-mile natural-gas transmission system that moves Permian Basin production from the Waha area to Agua Dulce and other South Texas markets. The system is fully subscribed under long-term binding transportation agreements and has approximately 2.59 Bcf/d of capacity following a June 2026 compression expansion. Kinder Morgan Texas Pipeline LLC owns 34% and operates GCX. ArcLight-managed vehicles own the remaining 66% through three separately recorded tranches acquired in 2022, 2024 and 2025. Mubadala's publicly disclosed co-investment is nested within ArcLight's 2025 tranche; its specific percentage and legal vehicle are not publicly disclosed and are not additive to ArcLight's 66% aggregate interest. No GCX-specific sale or pending exit was identified through August 13, 2026.

description: Permanent Power Company is a CIM Group-backed U.S. power-infrastructure platform that owns and develops utility-scale solar generation, battery storage and transmission assets. Westlands Solar Park is the California site/master plan beneath Permanent Power, and Aquamarine is its first 250 MW utility-scale solar project rather than a separate portfolio company. The Westlands development lineage began in 2014, construction started in 2020 and Aquamarine entered commercial operation in late 2021. description: Metrus Energy, Inc. is a U.S. Energy-as-a-Service platform that finances, owns, operates and maintains energy-efficiency, HVAC, lighting, water, solar and storage upgrades under long-term Sustainable Energy Services Agreements. Metrus-named project LLCs, financed equipment, installers, lenders, tax-equity providers and customers remain subordinate structures or counterparties rather than separate PortCos or platform owners. description: Arium Networks LLC is a U.S. small-cell, distributed-antenna-system and venue-network infrastructure platform created from Crown Castle's former Small Cell business. name: ACES Delta, LLC
description: ACES Delta, LLC is a clean-hydrogen production and underground salt-cavern storage platform in Delta, Utah. The 2019 joint venture is currently owned by Chevron-controlled Magnum Development, LLC as majority owner and Mitsubishi Power Americas, Inc. as minority owner; exact percentages are not publicly disclosed. Haddington Energy Partners III formerly owned the platform indirectly through Magnum and exited that position when Chevron acquired 100% of Magnum in 2023. Haddington ESP I separately manages construction equity in the ACES I project company, while GIC, Ontario Teachers', AIMCo and Manulife are investors in that fund rather than verified direct ACES Delta owners. The first stage comprises 220 MW of electrolysis and two salt caverns supporting more than 300 GWh of storage. All 40 electrolyzers were reported commissioned in the first quarter of 2026, with final start-up still expected later in 2026. No later platform sale or signed pending ownership transaction was identified through August 29, 2026.

milestones.event: Magnum Development and Mitsubishi Hitachi Power Systems announced the Advanced Clean Energy Storage joint venture that became ACES Delta.
The U.S. Department of Energy closed a US$504.4 million loan guarantee for the ACES I hydrogen-production and storage project; the facility is debt rather than equity ownership.

Haddington announced US$650 million of commitments to Haddington ESP I from GIC, Ontario Teachers', AIMCo and Manulife; the institutions invested as fund LPs, not as disclosed direct ACES Delta owners.
Chevron acquired 100% of Magnum Development from Haddington, obtaining a majority interest in ACES Delta; Mitsubishi Power Americas remained the minority joint-venture owner.
HydrogenPro reported that all 40 electrolyzers comprising the 220 MW first stage had been commissioned, while final project start-up remained expected in the second half of 2026.

description: Harrison Street–1547 Data Center & Connectivity Platform is the manager-level U.S. program through which Harrison Street and FifteenFortySeven Critical Systems Realty invest in and operate carrier hotels, colocation facilities and connectivity-focused data centers. The countable platform is a recurring multi-asset investment and operating program rather than one asserted umbrella legal entity; corporate 1547 is the operator and co-sponsor, not a company shown to be owned by Harrison Street. Wells was the first joint acquisition in 2020, Pittock followed in early 2021, Orangeburg and Cheyenne were included in the November 2021 four-asset portfolio acquisition, and South Bend was added in 2024. Separate title-holding, borrower, lease and project LLCs remain asset-level vehicles beneath the platform. Harrison Street's exact fund or managed account, both parties' ownership percentages and the private cap tables of individual SPVs are not publicly disclosed. CIM Group sold Midway/CHIL1, CHIL2, Orangeburg/ORNY1 and Wyoming/Cheyenne/CHWY1 to the Harrison Street–1547 joint venture in a four-asset acquisition that followed the parties' earlier Wells Building acquisition, expanding the relationship to six data centers while 1547 remained manager.

The partners added Union Station/SBIN1 in South Bend to the connectivity portfolio in September and AlohaNAP in October, when they described the joint national platform as exceeding one million square feet.

Harrison Street and 1547 announced full occupancy and further expansion at Orangeburg/ORNY1, a 232,000-square-foot facility on a 23-acre campus with 24 MW of provisioned power, confirming continuing joint platform activity.
Pittock Block added 302,200 square feet, 179 service providers, and one of the Northwest's two primary internet exchanges to the 1547-Harrison Street platform.
The buyers disclosed planned capacity and facility upgrades following the Union Station/South Bend acquisition.
The Cheyenne data center was fully leased to a national virtual infrastructure and IT services customer when 1547 and Harrison Street acquired the portfolio.

description: Skyway Concession Company LLC is the concessionaire and operator of the Chicago Skyway, a 7.8-mile, six-lane toll road linking Chicago's Dan Ryan Expressway with the Indiana Toll Road.
